source_text:
Τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ προσέχετε, ἵνα καὶ ὁ θεὸς ὑμῖν. ἀντίψυχον ἐγὼ τῶν ὑποτασσομένων τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, πρεσβυτέροις, διακόνοις: καὶ μετ’ αὐτῶν μοι τὸ μέρος γένοιτο σχεῖν ἐν θεῷ. συγκοπιᾶτε ἀλλήλοις, συναθλεῖτε, συντρέχετε, συμπάσχετε, συγκοιμᾶσθε. συνεγείρεσθε ὡς θεοῦ οἰκονόμοι καὶ πάρεδροι καὶ ὑπηρέται.
ἀρέσκετε ᾧ στρατεύεσθε, ἀφ̓ οὖ καὶ τὰ ὀψώνια κομίζεσθε: μή τις ὑμῶν δεσέρτωρ εὑρεθῇ. τὸ βάπτισμα ὑμῶν μενέτω ὡς ὅπλα, ἡ πίστις ὡς περικεφαλαία, ἡ ἀγάπη ὡς δόρυ. ἡ ὑπομονὴ ὡς πανοπλία. τὰ δεπόσιτα ὑμῶν τὰ ἔργα ὑμῶν, ἵνα τὰ ἄκκεπτα ὑμῶν ἄξια κομίσησθε. μακροθυμήσατε οὖν μετ’ ἀλλήλων ἐν πραότητι, ὡς ὁ θεὸς μεθ̓ ὑμῶν, ὀναίμην ὑμῶν διὰ παντός.
thought_title: Soldiers of God: heed the bishop and keep your equipment
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, urging them to unite under their bishop, elders, and deacons, and now gives them a series of military-style exhortations about shared labor and spiritual armor.
pass_a_gloss: Pay attention to the bishop, in order that God also may pay attention to you. I am a ransom on behalf of those who are subject to the bishop, council of elders (presbyters), deacons; and may it be granted to me to have a portion with them in God. Labor together with one another, struggle together, run together, suffer together, sleep together, be raised together, as God's stewards and assessors and servants. Please the one in whose army you serve, from whom you also receive your wages; let none of you be found a deserter. Let your baptism remain as weapons, faith as a helmet, love as a spear, endurance as full armor. Your deposits are your works, in order that you may receive your acceptable things worthily. Be patient therefore with one another in gentleness, as God is with you. May I have joy of you always.

choices.why: Ignatius offers his own life as a substitute on behalf of those who submit to the church order; 'ransom' captures the substitutionary force without implying a payment to anyone
The verb means to sleep or lie down together; in this sequence of shared activities, 'rest together' fits the rhythm of shared life without over-literalizing sleep
The term means those who sit beside, as assessors or attendants; 'assessors' preserves the official, court-like nuance of sitting beside God as his council
The Latin loanword means deposits or things entrusted; 'deposits' keeps the financial metaphor of works stored up for a return
The Latin loanword means things received or accepted; 'acceptable things' preserves the passive sense of what is received back as due reward

choices.english: may I have joy of you
choices.why: The optative of ὀνίνημι means to have profit or joy from someone; 'may I have joy of you' captures the warm personal wish Ignatius expresses

pass_b_english: Pay close attention to the bishop, so that God may pay close attention to you. I offer my very life for those who submit to the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons. May I be counted worthy to have a share with them in God. Labor together, struggle together, run together, suffer together, rest together, and rise together as God's stewards, counselors, and servants.

Please the one in whose army you serve, the one from whom you also receive your wages. Let none of you be found a deserter. Let your baptism remain as your armor, your faith as a helmet, your love as a spear, your endurance as full battle gear. Your works are your deposits, so that you may receive back what is due to you. Be patient with one another, then, in gentleness, as God is with you. May I have joy in you always.

problems.why: συγκοιμᾶσθε means 'sleep together' or 'lie down together', not 'rest together'; in context of resurrection theme, it anticipates death before rising.

problems.why: συνεγείρεσθε is passive 'be raised together' (resurrection), not active 'rise together'; this misses the theological passive and connection to Christ's resurrection.
